name: Smt. Sangeeta Gupta
tagline: Ex IRS, Abstract Artist, Poet, Filmmaker
bio: Sangeeta Gupta is a former Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, an 1984 batch IRS officer and a prominent Indian abstract artist, poet, and filmmaker.

Sangeeta Gupta's artistic journey spans 36 solo exhibitions of paintings. Her 36th solo exhibition Aadiyogi Shiv, a journey in cosmic indigo has travelled to 16 destinations in India and abroad. She has to her credit 35 published books.

Besides several National and international awards, she was also awarded a Doctor of Literature degree by the 42nd World Congress of Poets(2023) recognizing her outstanding contributions to the world of literature. Six of her documentary films are now part of the collection of the US Library of Congress, Washington."Song of the Cosmos" serves as her creative biography.

Sangeeta has created the world’s longest Indigo Painting on hand woven khadi titled Aadiyogi shiv : a journey in cosmic indigo. To promote sustainable living and natural indigo, she created this painting.Handmade fabric, natural colour and dye are chemical free and environment friendly. In March 2020, she created the world's longest textile painting with natural indigo colour extracted from the plant and finds a mention in Limca Book of records.
Aadiyogi Shiv : A journey in cosmic indigo series of paintings are born out of infinite, formless energy of Aadiyogi Shiv,Ardhnarishwar, the ultimate feminist.
There is no beginning, no end, all encompassing, omnipresent Shiv ispresent in all of us.

name: Smt. Aashima Mehrotra
tagline: Visual Artist and Executive Director Heritage-Ministry of Railway
bio: Based in the vibrant metropolis of Delhi, Aashima Mehrotra is a visual artist whose lifelong passion for art has been nurtured from an early age. Her artistic journey is intricately woven with her professional life as a civil servant, enriched by diverse experiences and travel that deepen her connection to the world. Her work embodies cosmic resonance, expressing the intricate vibrations linking human experiences to the universe's rhythm.

Inspired by luminaries such as Nandlal Bose, Amrita Sher-Gil, Picasso, and Vincent van Gogh, she draws from both traditional and contemporary influences. Although predominantly self-taught, she has refined her craft under the guidance of esteemed mentors like Veer Munshi, Shobha Broota, and Dharmapada Awardee Banshidhar Prahary. Impressionism and post-impressionism form her stylistic foundation, yet her creative evolution remains fluid, frequently exploring abstraction and mixed media.

Her compositions delve into metaphysical realms, intertwining elements of nature, memory, and dreamlike imagery. Each stroke of encaustic wax channels a deeper harmony between the material and ethereal. As a civil servant in the Railways and Tourism sectors, she has embraced the cultural and artistic diversity of Indian towns, further enriching her visual language.

Currently maintaining a studio at Lalit Kala, Garhi, her work is part of distinguished private collections, including those of notable figures such as Adil Hussain and Justice K. Kannan. Her artistic philosophy invites viewers to experience art as a conduit of universal resonance, reflecting a unique interplay of the sensory and the transcendental.

Aashima explores the vibratory nature of the universe through her captivating Cosmic Energy series. Among the world’s most powerful sources of healing vibrations is the ancient city of Varanasi, a place steeped in rich spiritual resonance. She seeks to convey how positive vibrations can manifest in various forms—through sacred spaces, and the energies of our surroundings.

name: Smt. Nidhi Chaudhuri
tagline: IAS, Director of National Gallery of Modern Art, Mumbai.
bio: Nidhi Chaudhuri is an expressive artist whose work embodies a deep connection to her consciousness through vibrant colors and diverse forms. She creates energy paintings, spiritual art, landscapes, and abstracts using oil and acrylics, allowing her intuition to guide her artistic journey. Nidhi embraces fluidity in her practice, eschewing fixed styles and rigid mediums to convey the call of her soul across the canvas.

She holds an Advanced Diploma in Fine Arts from the Bombay Art Society in Bandra, where she honed her skills and artistic vision. Nidhi's work has been showcased in notable exhibitions, including a prominent show at the Jio World Centre in Mumbai in 2022. In 2023, she participated in several significant events, such as the PL Deshpandey Exhibition at Ravindra Natya Mandir, the India Art Festival at Nehru Centre, and the Art Carnival of the Bombay Art Society, among others. Her art was also featured in a group show at Ahmedabad ni Gufa Art Gallery.

Looking ahead, Nidhi is set to hold a solo exhibition at the State Goods & Services Tax Office in 2024, alongside participation in the India Art Festival in New Delhi and further exhibitions in Mumbai. Through her art, Nidhi continues to explore and express the interplay between energy, spirituality, and the natural world.

Nidhi Chaudhary's painting series featuring dervish swirling captures the mesmerizing fluidity and spiritual essence of Sufi dance. Through subtle colors and dynamic brushwork, she conveys the transformative energy of movement, inviting viewers to experience the profound connection between art and spirituality.

name: Abhay Kumar
tagline: Poet, Editor, Translator, Artist, Deputy Director General ICCR
bio: Abhay Kumar (pen name Abhay K.) is an esteemed Indian poet, diplomat, editor, translator, anthologist, and artist, currently serving as the Deputy Director General of the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) in New Delhi. His influential poetry collection, Earth Anthem, has been translated into over 150 languages and was presented at the United Nations to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Earth Day.

Abhay's significant contributions to contemporary South Asian poetry earned him the SAARC Literary Award, and he was nominated for the Pushcart Prize in 2013. He also received the Asia-Pacific Excellence Award in 2014 and has been recognized as a "World Poet" by Pulitzer Prize-winning poet Vijay Seshadri. Notably, his poem "The Partitioned Land" was included in the curriculum at Cornell University in Fall 2021, and his book-length poem Monsoon has been selected for study by Harvard University’s assistant professor Sarah Dimick as part of a project on climate and literature.

In addition to his literary achievements, Abhay's artistic works explore geometric forms and the evolution of planetary consciousness. He has exhibited his paintings in solo exhibitions across the globe, including cities like St. Petersburg, Paris, New Delhi, Brasília, and Antananarivo. Through his multifaceted talents, Abhay Kumar continues to bridge art and diplomacy, fostering cultural dialogue on a global scale.

Abhay's works in his series Shoonya are visualizations of emptiness. Forms are visible when one looks at them closely but as one moves away from them, forms disappear and what remains is emptiness, a true validation of the crux of the Heart Sutra: ‘Form is emptiness, emptiness is form.’

name: Zuzana Mezencevová
bio: Zuzana Mezencevová (b. 1969) is a Slovak diplomat currently serving at the Embassy of the Slovak Republic in New Delhi. Originally from Košice, Slovakia, she returned to her passion for painting in 2007 while working as a contributing editor for one of Slovakia’s oldest national weekly magazines. Mezencevová has a particular affinity for watercolours, appreciating their spontaneity and vibrant colour potential. Recently, she has expanded her artistic repertoire to include digital painting, particularly in the context of urban sketching.

Her work has been showcased in exhibitions across Slovakia, Austria, Italy, and India, reflecting a diverse cultural influence. As a member of the visual artists' association arte.via, based in Stupava, Slovakia, and a regular participant in Urban Sketchers Delhi since 2017, she engages with fellow artists and the broader community, sharing her unique perspective on urban life through art.

Mezencevová's artistic journey, intertwined with her diplomatic career, highlights her commitment to exploring and expressing the beauty of everyday moments, whether through traditional media or modern digital tools. Her ability to capture the essence of urban environments continues to resonate with audiences, making her a significant contributor to the contemporary art scene.

All the works draw inspiration from nature and the creative process itself. Water and movement are essential, guiding the pigments as they flow across the canvas. For Zuzana, the act of painting is a healing journey. She often listen to light music, which makes the flow of her work meditative.

name: Ragini Upadhyay
tagline: A distinguished Nepalese artist and the first woman Chancellor of the Nepal Academy of Fine Arts
bio: Ragini Upadhyay is a distinguished Nepalese artist and the first woman Chancellor of the Nepal Academy of Fine Arts (2014-2018). She earned her Fine Arts degree from Lucknow College of Arts, India, in 1982, and has since been recognized internationally for her contributions to printmaking, including fellowships at prestigious institutions in the UK and Germany.

Throughout her career, Upadhyay has garnered numerous accolades, including multiple National Awards and the Late King and Queen – Birendra Aishwarya Memorial Medal in 2002. Her artistic excellence was further acknowledged with the Kate and Robert Wilson Prize in 1984 and the Best Award at the 100 years of Lucknow College of Arts in 2011, among others.

An influential educator, she has lectured at esteemed institutions in Finland and Pakistan and has conducted talks globally, including at the Helsingborg Museum in Sweden and Bridgewater State University in the USA.

With 70 solo exhibitions across countries such as Austria, Japan, and Nepal, her works are housed in prestigious collections including the SAARC Building in Kathmandu and the World Bank museum in the USA. Upadhyay's art not only reflects her rich heritage but also bridges cultural dialogues across borders, making her a pivotal figure in contemporary art. Her dedication to her craft and contributions to the arts have left a lasting impact both in Nepal and internationally.

Her series Ashes is a powerful collection of paintings was born out of deep personal loss and a profound desire to reconnect with her beloved daughter Shivata and her mother, whom she lost within the same year. Through her art, Ragini transforms her grief into a poignant exploration of life, death, and the bonds that transcend time.

name: Indu Tripathy
tagline: An acclaimed artist, her artwork is rooted in meditation and mindfulness.
bio: Indu Tripathy is an acclaimed artist known for her gentle, silken forms and soft colour palettes. Her work, often centered on the themes of womanhood and nature, reflects a deep connection between the two, presenting them as manifestations of prakriti. Indu's modernism is rooted in her cultural heritage and her holistic understanding of existence. Her portrayals of women exude a dreamy quality, capturing both their inherent strength and the complex narratives of gender.

Indu holds an M.A. in Fine Art from Agra College and has garnered several prestigious awards, including a Senior Fellowship from the Department of Culture, Government of India. Her artworks are part of significant collections both in India and internationally. She resides and works in New Delhi.

Her professional journey includes teaching Drawing and Painting at the Home Science Institute in Agra, serving as an illustrator for Delhi Press, and working with The Way Advertising. She has contributed to notable projects, including designing tableaux for the Indian Air Force and stalls for Orissa Tourism. Additionally, Indu has played key roles in organizing art workshops and has been involved in various jury panels, further enriching her commitment to the arts.

Since 2000, Indu Tripathi has been conducting art classes in Sainik Farms and Defence Colony, sharing her passion and expertise with aspiring artists. Her multifaceted career showcases her dedication to both creating and nurturing art in the community.

Indu Tripathy's artwork is rooted in meditation and mindfulness, allowing people to experience a sense of calm. Each piece is created with deliberate intention, using soft colors and flowing forms that encourage reflection and inner peace. The process of creating is as transformative as the final work, allowing her to connect deeply with the present moment.

name: Dr. Lakshman Prasad
tagline: Associate Professor of Painting at the School of Performing and Visual Arts
bio: Dr. Lakshman Prasad is an Associate Professor of Painting at the School of Performing and Visual Arts, Indira Gandhi National Open University, where he specializes in visual arts. With over 14 years of teaching experience, he has significantly contributed to the education and development of aspiring artists.

Dr. Prasad's work has been recognized both nationally and internationally. He received the prestigious award at the 10th International Biennial of Miniature Art in Czestochowa, Poland, in 2018, showcasing his talent on a global platform. His national accolades include multiple awards from the Lalit Kala Akademi and the Camel Art Foundation, affirming his status as a leading figure in contemporary Indian art.

Throughout his career, Dr. Prasad has participated in numerous exhibitions, including the 58th National Exhibition of Art in New Delhi and the 28th National Exhibition of Contemporary Art in Nagpur, where he received sponsorship for a solo exhibition. His commitment to his craft is further demonstrated through various accolades, such as the North Zone Bronze Award from the Prafulla Foundation and a Certificate of Merit from the All India Art Exhibition.
Dr. Prasad's dedication to painting and education continues to inspire his students and the broader art community, making him a significant contributor to the field of visual arts in India.

Laxman Prasad's depiction of Buddha is a celebration of stillness and wisdom. Through bold textures and subtle hues, he tries to convey a sense of serene strength and compassion. Each element is thoughtfully composed, inviting viewers to immerse themselves in a moment of reflection and spiritual connection.

name: Amit Kalla
tagline: An acclaimed poet and painter from Jaipur, blends spiritual symbolism and semiotics in his abstract art
bio: Amit Kalla, born on February 7, 1980, in Jaipur, is an acclaimed poet and painter. He holds a Master’s in Art and Aesthetics from Jawaharlal Nehru University and a Master’s in Drawing and Painting from Rajasthan University. He is pursuing a Ph.D. on “Spiritual Symbolism and Semiotics in Indian Abstract Paintings.” His work, shaped by travels across 15 countries, blends spiritual depth with abstract art. Kalla has published four poetry collections, including the Jnanpith Young Poet Award-winning Hone Na Hone Se Pare. His accolades include the prestigious Mark Rothko Residency Award (2022), and participation in major art exhibitions and international poetry festivals. With 14 solo exhibitions and over 150 group shows, Kalla’s art explores themes of universality and cultural introspection. He is also active in social change through art initiatives like the Ramta Drig Collective, Jaipur Art Summit & pink Fest.
The In Within series captures the ever-evolving patterns of energy, akin to the flow of prana in yoga.

Amit Kalla's forms, often symbolic silhouettes, dissolve into abstract backgrounds, resembling effects that reflect light and create a fantastical visual experience. This interplay echoes the balance sought in meditation—a harmony between thought and stillness.

name: Dr. Nivedita Bandil
tagline: A dentist, painter, and poetess from Mumbai. An accomplished artist, she creates vibrant works that includes portraits. landscapes. and modern art
bio: Dr. Nivedita Bandil is a dentist, painter, and poetess. An accomplished artist, she creates vibrant works that include portraits, landscapes, and modern art, with a special passion for depicting Krishna and Radha in various forms. Her paintings have received widespread acclaim and popularity. She is also the author of her recently published poetry book, “अंतर्द्वंद,” which has captivated poetry lovers. Despite being diagnosed with Parkinson's three years ago, Dr. Nivedita continues to paint, and her acrylic works reflect a freshness that transports observers into a realm of divinity.

Nivedita's painting of Radha and Krishna captures the essence of divine love and devotion. Through vibrant colors and intricate details, she aims to evoke the joyous connection between the two, to experience a sense of spiritual unity and transcendence. Each brushstroke reflects the depth of their bond, celebrating the beauty of love in its purest form.

name: Dr. Nitin Madan (P.C.S)
tagline: A distinguished civil servant, currently serving as the Additional District Magistrate (Administration) in Uttar Pradesh
bio: Dr. Nitin Madan (P.C.S) Dr. Nitin Madan is a distinguished civil servant, currently serving as the Additional District Magistrate (Administration) in Uttar Pradesh. With over a decade of experience in public administration, disaster management, and law enforcement, he is dedicated to fostering transparent, efficient governance and community development. Dr. Madan holds a PhD in Mathematics from M.J.P. Rohilkhand University and was a Gold Medalist in Mathematics from Hindu College, Moradabad. He has served in various key administrative roles, like sub divisional magistrate,Additional Municipal Commissioner etc. Presently he is a Class-1 P.C.S. Officer. In addition to his professional accomplishments, Dr. Madan is passionate about the arts, particularly drawing, where he specializes in graphite and charcoal. His artistic practice serves as an important outlet for creativity, and he finds it a valuable means of personal expression.

name: Anand Bekwad
tagline: A Pune based artist captures the vibrant essence of Varanasi through his joyful and colourful renditions.
bio: Anand Bekwad, a Pune based artist, captures the vibrant essence of Varanasi through his joyful and colourful renditions. His Artwork reflect the dynamic energy and cultural richness of this ancient city. With Multiple solo and group exhibitions across India, Anand’s creations offer a unique perspective to the timeless allure of the Ancient City Varanasi.

Anand draws inspiration from the ancient city of Varanasi, using contemporary forms of paintings, he portrays the city anew, keeping its spiritual energy alive with his strokes and colours, almost inviting people to explore the ancient wisdom it offers.

name: Tarun Sharma
tagline: A multifaceted artist from Jaipur, blending the worlds of painting, poetry, and design thinking to foster a mind-liberating approach to creativity.
bio: Tarun Sharma is a multifaceted artist, blending the worlds of painting, poetry, and design thinking to foster a mind-liberating approach to creativity. Born in July 1985 in Jaipur and raised in Udaipur, Rajasthan, Tarun's upbringing in a nature-rich environment deeply influenced his artistic vision. He studied Architecture at VNIT Nagpur and further pursued Transportation and Automobile Design at NID, Ahmedabad.

His artistic journey evolved from doodling and working with various materials to focusing on canvas in 2012, where abstraction became central to his work. Tarun's art draws inspiration from Indian knowledge systems, exploring themes of consciousness, energy, and the essence of being.

He held his first solo exhibition at Cercles in New Delhi in December 2015, followed by another at Devang, Tolstoy House. Tarun has participated in several group exhibitions, including “Explorations” at AIFACS and “Noir” at The Stainless Gallery, both in New Delhi, as well as “Chaap” at Jawahar Kala Kendra in Jaipur. His work reflects a unique synthesis of his diverse experiences, aiming to engage viewers in a dialogue about the deeper aspects of existence.

In Tarun's series Naad, we find symbols of creation, the energy, the conscious, the energy. To be meditated upon, stroke by stroke, holding the attention in process of creation these works are a signifier of the source denoted by the symbol.
